title: arXiv Mathematics — 3 November 2026
global_caveat: arXiv supplies no official trending chart: this is an inferred ordering, not a popularity ranking, and same-day preprints have little citation evidence.

sections.title: Construction of the 2D non-Abelian Yang-Mills-Higgs measure via stochastic quantisation
sections.abstract: The authors construct the non-Abelian Yang–Mills–Higgs measure on a two-dimensional torus by stochastic quantisation, proving global well-posedness, uniform-in-time bounds, and a unique invariant measure for the associated flow on gauge orbits.
sections.claimed_result: The authors report that, for the stochastic Yang–Mills–Higgs flow, a gauge-covariant approximation converges after renormalisation to a globally well-posed flow that is topologically irreducible and strong Feller; hence it has a unique invariant probability measure defining the sought measure.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Two-dimensional torus; compact connected Lie group, finite-dimensional orthogonal Higgs representation, and fixed coupling parameters; the paper works in distributional gauge-orbit spaces with a sufficiently small regularity parameter.
sections.unique_caveat: This is a 350-page preprint, and the measure is constructed in the stated two-dimensional setting, not for arbitrary manifolds or dimensions; the extensive analytic argument has not been independently assessed here.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Three-way cross-listing across PDE, mathematical physics, and probability; the abstract claims a first construction for this model. A Warwick stochastic-analysis seminar listing for Wenhao Zhao on 28 Oct 2026 is an independent, checkable discussion signal.

sections.title: Local scaling limit of the four-dimensional uniform spanning tree
sections.abstract: The author proves that the wired uniform spanning tree of Z^4, viewed from the origin, converges locally to a spatial Brownian Kesten tree, jointly tracking intrinsic distance, volume, and Euclidean embedding, with logarithmic rescalings.
sections.claimed_result: The author proves local rooted spatial Gromov-weak convergence to a Brownian spine with independent spatial Brownian trees grafted at constant rate, and convergence of the rescaled space-time occupation measure to infinite canonical super-Brownian motion.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The wired uniform spanning forest on Z^4, rooted at the origin; distance, volume, and spatial positions are rescaled jointly using dimension-four logarithmic corrections.
sections.unique_caveat: The result is specific to the critical four-dimensional lattice model and its stated local topology; the scaling constants alpha and kappa are not individually known explicitly (the paper gives their product).
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The paper addresses the critical four-dimensional case left open by earlier scaling-limit results and gives a concrete continuum object plus sharp first-moment asymptotics. The abstract’s claim is a substantial probability result, rather than evidence of measured readership.

sections.title: A proof of the spectral rigidity for complex projective space
sections.abstract: The authors claim that, among compact connected Kähler manifolds, the spectrum with multiplicities of the Hodge Laplacian in any one fixed degree determines complex projective space with its Fubini–Study metric up to holomorphic isometry.
sections.claimed_result: The authors prove the one-fixed-degree Hodge-spectrum rigidity statement and outline a chain using periodic geodesic flow, integral cohomology, heat coefficients, wave traces, and Kähler geometry.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Compact connected Kähler manifold without boundary, with the Hodge-Laplacian spectrum including multiplicities equal to that of CP^n in a single fixed degree 0 <= p <= n; the conclusion is holomorphic isometry to the Fubini–Study model.
sections.unique_caveat: This is a technically long preprint; the universal claim depends on handling exceptional dimension pairs by additional wave-trace and topological arguments, which have not been independently checked here.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: A precise rigidity theorem addressing a stated folklore conjecture, with a strong one-spectrum conclusion for every fixed pair (p,n), is a notable geometric result; no attention or citation metric is used for its placement.

sections.title: Near-optimal bounds for the critical 2d SHF and the delta-Bose gas
sections.abstract: The authors improve the upper bound on the N-th moment of the critical two-dimensional stochastic heat flow to exp(exp(C N^(1+o(1)))), bringing it close to the known lower bound and identifying the exponential scale predicted for the delta-Bose gas.
sections.claimed_result: The authors establish near-optimal upper and lower exponential scales for the critical 2D stochastic heat-flow moments, and for each fixed N express the delta-Bose ground-state energy through the bottom of a principal-operator spectrum.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Critical two-dimensional stochastic heat flow and the two-dimensional N-body delta-Bose gas; the spectral formula is stated for each fixed N.
sections.unique_caveat: The result reaches the conjectured exponential scale only up to a vanishing error in the exponent; the abstract does not claim a full resolution of Rajeev’s conjecture.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Three-way probability/physics/functional-analysis cross-listing and a quantified improvement from an N^2 exponent to N^(1+o(1)), compared in the abstract with an existing lower bound.

sections.title: The proof of the Harary--Hill conjecture: a detailed exposition and an extension to rotation systems
sections.abstract: The author presents a combinatorial exposition of a reported proof of the Harary–Hill crossing-number conjecture and proves a more general weighted inequality for rotation systems of complete graphs.
sections.claimed_result: The author proves that every rotation system of K_n has at least Z(n) when one counts realizable four-vertex subsystems with weight one and non-realizable ones with weight three; the Harary–Hill formula follows.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Complete graph K_n, n >= 3, and an arbitrary rotation system; the paper’s main inequality is combinatorial and does not require a drawing of the graph.
sections.unique_caveat: The author explicitly frames this as an exposition of a proof uploaded elsewhere, rather than the original discovery; the underlying proof’s correctness is not independently established by the existence of this explanatory preprint.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The conjecture proof has independent public discussion, including an earlier arXiv exposition and a mathematical commentary; this paper adds a stated rotation-system generalisation. The discussion signal is about the underlying proof, not evidence that this exposition has been peer reviewed.

sections.title: Improved lower bounds for the kissing number in dimensions 49 to 61
sections.abstract: The author gives explicit sphere-contact configurations improving the previously published kissing-number lower bound in every dimension from 49 through 61, with exact-integer certificates and code/data linked from the paper.
sections.claimed_result: The author reports improvements over prior published lower bounds in all 13 dimensions, totaling 506,461 additional points across the stated configurations, verified in exact integer arithmetic.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Kissing configurations in Euclidean R^d, 49 <= d <= 61; constructions use an antipodal block lift of a large lattice shell and computer-assisted local/greedy search, with code and certificates linked in the arXiv record.
sections.unique_caveat: These are lower bounds, not proofs of the exact kissing numbers; the search certifies the listed configurations but not their optimality.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Cross-listed in metric geometry, information theory, and combinatorics; the improvement covers 13 dimensions and the abstract links reproducible construction data and exact certificates.

sections.title: $C^1$-rigidity of $\mathbb{H}^{p,q}$-convex cocompact representations of Gromov hyperbolic groups
sections.abstract: The author proves that specified convex-cocompact representations with a continuously differentiable limit set must preserve a totally geodesic hyperbolic subspace, forcing the quotient representation to be virtually a cocompact hyperbolic lattice in the stated cases.
sections.claimed_result: For p>3, a non-elementary hyperbolic group with boundary S^(p-1) and the stated H^(p,2)-convex cocompact representation with C^1 proximal limit set preserves H^p; for odd p, the paper extends the conclusion to signatures p>q>=2.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The group boundary must be a sphere of dimension p-1; the representation is convex cocompact and its proximal limit set is a C^1 submanifold. The broader arbitrary-signature conclusion is non-Zariski-density, not the full lattice conclusion.
sections.unique_caveat: The strongest conclusion has the listed dimension, signature, and boundary hypotheses; it should not be read as rigidity for arbitrary hyperbolic-group representations.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Four-way cross-listing across geometry, dynamics, group theory, and geometric topology, together with a classification-style rigidity conclusion under a clear regularity hypothesis.

sections.title: Efficient congruencing in $\mathbb Z[t]$ modulo $t^2$
sections.abstract: The author develops nested efficient congruencing over the truncated polynomial ring Z[t]/(t^2) and proves a Vinogradov-type mean-value bound under a non-vanishing Wronskian condition.
sections.claimed_result: If the polynomial Wronskian is nonzero modulo t and 1 <= s <= k(k+1)/2, the counted integral solutions satisfy Upsilon_{s,k}(X;phi) << X^(2s+epsilon); the author outlines extensions and applications.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Polynomials phi_j(u) in Z[t,u], the stated Wronskian condition, and the stated range of s; variables obey |u_i|, |v_i| <= X, with constants implicit in the bound.
sections.unique_caveat: The estimate is conditional on the Wronskian and range restrictions; the abstract describes some broader applications as forthcoming rather than proved in this paper.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: A concrete quantitative estimate extends an established number-theoretic method to a nonstandard ring, and the abstract points to number-field and function-field variants; ranking reflects the result’s scope, not observed readership.
